key_insight: A single natural-language serialization of all patient data can power one pretrained language model to handle multimodal clinical prediction without custom fusion architectures.
clinical_relevance: This could simplify deployment across clinical tasks by reducing engineering complexity while matching or outperforming specialized multimodal and existing clinical models.
method: Convert structured EHR variables and free-text notes into one text sequence.
Fine-tune encoder- and decoder-based pretrained language models end-to-end.
Compare against task-specific multimodal baselines and a clinical gradient-boosting system for graft failure.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three tasks—MIMIC-III in-hospital mortality, German transplant graft failure prediction, and ambulance triage classification—where unified text-based models matched or exceeded multimodal baselines and beat the deployed graft-failure gradient boosting model.
watch_item: Performance was shown on specific datasets and tasks, so real-world robustness, calibration, and generalization across institutions still need validation.
paper_title: Large Language Models as Unified Multimodal Learners for Clinical Prediction
